findings.description: The review diff honours `refs/replace/*`, which lives in the shared common dir the session writes. A session can `git replace` its malicious blob or tip commit with a harmless one, so the xhigh reviewer reads harmless code while `pup merge --pr` pushes the real objects. The command needs `--no-replace-objects`.
findings.body:
[`SECURITY_REVIEW_DIFF`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/5b04aad077f89cba3e2a180cf121774fd6fd45d3/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L570-L577) now pins both ends to `refs/heads/`. But git still swaps in objects from `refs/replace/*` on every normal read, and this command passes none of `--no-replace-objects`, `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS` or `core.useReplaceRefs=false`. Nothing else in the repo does either.

`refs/replace/` sits in the shared `$GIT_COMMON_DIR`. Decisions 41, 54 and 80 already treat that directory as something the session can write. The attack:
1. The session commits malicious content.
2. It runs `git replace <blob-or-tip> <benign>`.
3. `git diff refs/heads/<target>...refs/heads/pup/<id>` prints the benign content.

[`pushBranch`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/5b04aad077f89cba3e2a180cf121774fd6fd45d3/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L1499-L1530) pushes the pinned sha from inside `withScratchGitDir`. That scratch dir has no `refs/replace`, so the PR carries the real objects, which the xhigh subagent never saw. `--text`, `--no-textconv` and the `refs/heads/` pin don't help, because the swap happens below the diff machinery.

On git 2.19 to 2.42, a `core.useReplaceRefs=true` planted in the shared config can override the command-line flag. So pin the config key as well; a `-c` on the command line beats the repo config on every version. Update the pinned string at `src/core/profile-compiler.test.ts:950` and decision 92's sentence to match.

(Context, not in scope for this line: `cutGateCheckout` reads the tree through `runGit`, which also honours replacements, so a replaced tip would also make build, test and lint run on the benign tree.)

findings.description: The session can set `core.worktree` to an ancestor directory and `diff.relative=true` in the shared config. The review diff, run with `-C .worktrees/<session-id>`, then shows only paths under a prefix such as `<session-id>/`, so the real changes disappear. The command needs `--no-relative`.
findings.body:
`diff.relative=true` (git ≥ 2.28) limits every porcelain `git diff` to paths under the cwd's prefix inside the work tree, tree-to-tree `A...B` diffs included. On its own it does nothing here, because `-C .worktrees/<session-id>` is normally the worktree root and the prefix is empty.

The session can change the work tree root. Git ignores `core.worktree` in the shared config for a linked worktree. But once `extensions.worktreeConfig` is set in the shared config, git reads `core.worktree` from `.git/worktrees/<id>/config.worktree`. The repo's own tests use that exact path (`src/core/git-diff-client.test.ts:381-390`, `src/core/merge-gate.test.ts:1426-1435`). Decision 92's text treats a planted `core.worktree` as a real threat, and that is why the gate passes `--work-tree` (`merge-gate.service.ts:357, 619`).

The attack:
1. Point the worktree's `core.worktree` at `.worktrees/` or at the repo root.
2. Set `diff.relative=true`.
3. The cwd is now `<id>/` or `.worktrees/<id>/` inside the work tree, so the [review command](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/5b04aad077f89cba3e2a180cf121774fd6fd45d3/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L575-L576) prints only changes under that prefix.

The output is empty, or a decoy the session committed at that path. The session can plant both keys after its last commit and remove them before `pup merge`.

`--no-relative` overrides the config. `-c diff.relative=false` would also work on gits older than 2.28. Update the pinned string at `src/core/profile-compiler.test.ts:950` and decision 92 to match.

findings.description: Decision 92 still says the review runs "over the worktree's `main...HEAD` diff", while two lines later the same sentence says it runs between `refs/heads/<target>` and `refs/heads/pup/<session-id>`; drop or reword the stale `main...HEAD` clause so the decision matches the code.

The line "session writes the shared git config, attributes and tags and can move its worktree HEAD. `runUtility`" is about 105 characters, past the ~100-column wrap of the surrounding lines; move `` `runUtility` `` to the next line.
